instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil if you like.

Meanwhile, trim the Brussels sprouts and cut them in half, leaving any small ones whole. Peel the carrots and slice them on an angle about 1/2 inch thick. Halve the red onion and slice it 1/4 inch thick.
Put the vegetables straight onto the baking sheet. Add 3 tbsp olive oil, the 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper and toss with your hands until everything is shiny.
Tuck the sausage links in between the vegetables with space around each one, and spread the vegetables into a single layer as best you can. Turn the Brussels sprouts cut side down.

Roast for 25 minutes without stirring, until the sausages are browned and the vegetables are tender with dark edges. You're cooking the sausage to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, chop a small handful of the parsley.
Drizzle the 2 tsp red wine vinegar over the hot vegetables and toss them on the pan. Scatter the parsley over everything.
Taste a sprout. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or another splash of the vinegar.
Serve with the red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions toss the vegetables with oil, salt, pepper and dried herbs right on the sheet, spread them in a single layer around whole sausage links and roast until the sausage is cooked and the vegetables are browned. Once Upon a Chef uses red onion, carrots and Brussels sprouts with thyme at 425°F for 25 minutes without stirring; Girl Heart Food uses bell peppers and baby potatoes with garlic powder, paprika, oregano and cayenne at 400°F, stirs and flips halfway, and finishes with red wine vinegar, parsley and red pepper flakes. This follows Once Upon a Chef with sweet sausage for a mild pan, and borrows Girl Heart Food's vinegar and parsley finish with the pepper flakes on the side.
